changes.rationale: October 30 issuer-distributed release announces CMS pass-through reimbursement for Omidria effective January 2015. Review judgment: class 7 equivalent government coverage/payment authorization, distinct from FDA product approval granted earlier. Retain existing same-session reimbursement attribution; no new trial claim.

October 9 issuer release announces final CMS national coverage determination; October 10 market report says announcement was late Thursday and attributes Friday gains to it. Class 7 equivalent coverage authorization, not a new FDA approval. Final coverage and preliminary pricing are separate decisions.

October 11 issuer release establishes 2014 deployment forecast of 475–525 MW versus reaffirmed 2013 target of 278 MW. Review judgment: standalone next-year operating outlook is the primary catalyst, with retrospective deployment metrics, proposed financing and Zep acquisition as concurrent context; not a routine quarterly financial-results report.

February 8 market account attributes Caesars and peers rally to Las Vegas industry revenue data and New Jersey governor support for online gaming. Industry-policy repricing rather than an issuer-specific license, regulatory approval or contract.

May 17 market account identifies follow-through on the $500 million Goldman financing announced the day before, with an earlier-session rise already observed. Retain financing exclusion; do not treat financing capacity alone as a new customer contract.

July 14 issuer release reports already-completed Q2 EV sales and says full quarterly financial results will follow in August. Retrospective sales-volume update; no new award, order, partnership, product launch, technical breakthrough or forward guidance step-change is established.

May 2 contemporaneous account attributes the move to Oppenheimer upgrade and an accelerated-approval thesis. This does not establish an actual regulatory approval or successful clinical readout that day.

October 5 market-gainers report attributes Corbus move to Cantor Fitzgerald coverage initiation with Buy rating and $17 target. Upcoming readouts are expectations rather than newly reported trial success.

March 26 follow-up says CEO clarified that the automaker order hinted at on March 25 had already been disclosed with March 13 earnings. Do not label re-publicized order commentary as a newly established class 5 contract.

Primary issuer-distributed first-patient glucose-clamp release is April 1, twelve days before the recorded jump. Correct prior implication of same-day enrollment news. Enrollment itself is not a successful trial readout; independent April 13 cause remains unverified.

Emergency investor-call account mixes 2015 profitability/revenue commentary, proposed repurchases, staffing cuts and Ocwen reassurances. A class 8 outlook event is possible, but no quantified change versus prior outlook or completed regulatory resolution is established in this review.

Primary outlook release is January 14; newswire index timestamps it 06:15 ET before that session opened. January 15 cannot be assumed to be first reaction to that announcement. Defer for a fresh catalyst search or continuation attribution.

Syndicated holiday-guidance release has January 13 internal dateline and January 19 hosting date, both preceding January 21 jump. Do not use republication date as first-public timing. Need independent same-session evidence before class 8.

June 25 primary release confirms favorable IRS rulings enabling REIT conversion, with distribution and outlook changes. Legal-unlock category is plausible; exact release time is not recovered here, so June 26 reaction assignment remains pending.

Existing locator is a September 5 Neonode market article, not July 10 contemporaneous evidence. A design-win/license could qualify as class 5/6, but source/date mismatch prevents a supported promotion.

June 24 market account links June 23 move to CNN/CEO discussion of a tier-one license, but also points to similar disclosure in March 9 earnings call. Partnership substance is plausible; novelty and earlier-public conflict need resolution before keep. No counterparty identity is inferred.

limitations: No database-derived snapshot or saved news queue refreshed.
Existing price attribution retained unless a conflict is explicitly deferred.
No exhaustive earlier-public search; no training or evaluation gates unlocked.
